config.notes: Human goal: implement medterm4ds integration in 4 sequential phases per fhir4ds-private/docs/plans/medterm4ds-integration.md. Each phase = feature_design -> feature_implementation -> code_review cycle. USER_DIRECTIVES.md pre-approves all phases (existing plan is the starting point; do NOT redesign from scratch). Auto-advance through all 12 pipeline steps. Track active phase via config.medterm4ds_phase (1..4). Target version 0.0.11. Zero-dep default is non-negotiable: fhir4ds core must import without medterm4ds/httpx/medspacy. Conformance must remain at 2822/2822 baseline. A Release Engineer artifact gate is required after Phase 4 before final completion (wheel rebuild likely needed).

issues.evidence: fhir4ds/cql/terminology/factory.py:69 + fhir4ds/cql/terminology/http_adapter.py:19 — The factory imports `from .http_adapter import HTTPTerminologyEndpoint` (line 69) BEFORE the `try: import httpx except ImportError` block at lines 71-77. Because http_adapter.py line 19 has `import httpx` at module top, when httpx is missing the ImportError is raised by line 19 with message 'import of httpx halted; None in sys.modules' — the factory's clean install hint ('Install with: pip install fhir4ds-v2[terminology]') is NEVER raised. The factory's try/except on lines 71-77 is dead code. Verified live by poisoning sys.modules['httpx']=None and calling the factory. Proposed fix: reorder the factory so the httpx presence check runs FIRST and the adapter is imported inside the try block (or move `import httpx` out of http_adapter.py module top into the methods that use it, matching the in_process adapter's lazy-import discipline).
issues.resolution: Moved httpx import out of http_adapter.py module top into a lazy _require_httpx() helper called inside _client(); factory try/except now surfaces the install hint correctly.

issues.evidence: fhir4ds/cql/tests/unit/terminology/test_factory.py:62-70 — `test_http_mode_without_httpx_raises_importerror` only passes when another test in the same session has already imported http_adapter (caching it in sys.modules). When run in isolation (`pytest test_factory.py::test_http_mode_without_httpx_raises_importerror`), it FAILS with 'AssertionError: Regex pattern did not match' (Regex: 'fhir4ds-v2\[terminology\]' vs Input: 'import of httpx halted; None in sys.modules'). This test-order pollution masks REV-001 and gives false confidence in the install-hint path. Proposed fix: after fixing REV-001, also clear sys.modules['fhir4ds.cql.terminology.http_adapter'] in the test fixture so the test is hermetic regardless of execution order.
issues.resolution: Test fixture now also clears sys.modules["fhir4ds.cql.terminology.http_adapter"] via monkeypatch.delitem so the lazy import is re-executed regardless of test order.
issues.verified_in: pytest fhir4ds/cql/tests/unit/terminology/test_factory.py::test_http_mode_without_httpx_raises_importerror -v (passes both in isolation and in full suite)

issues.spec_citation: docs/architecture/plans/FEATURE_MEDTERM4DS_PHASE1_TERMINOLOGY.md line 201: 'Normalize CodeRef.system via SystemResolver.normalize() before returning.'
issues.evidence: fhir4ds/cql/terminology/in_process_adapter.py:208 — `search_text` reads `system = getattr(code_obj, 'source', None)` and passes it through `_normalize_system()` → `SystemResolver.normalize()`. medterm4ds exposes `code.source` as a source mnemonic ('SNOMEDCT_US', 'RXNORM', 'LNC', 'ICD10CM') — NOT a FHIR canonical URL. SystemResolver.normalize() is a no-op for these strings (verified: returns input unchanged), so the resulting CodeRef.system='SNOMEDCT_US' will silently fail to join against valueset_codes rows that use 'http://snomed.info/sct'. The test test_search_text_returns_results codifies the bug by asserting r.system == 'SNOMEDCT_US'. Proposed fix: add a mnemonic→URL expansion map in the in_process adapter and apply it inside _normalize_system BEFORE calling SystemResolver.normalize; OR extend SystemResolver with a mnemonic map (mirroring its existing OID→URL map). Update the test assertion to expect the FHIR URL.
issues.resolution: Added _SOURCE_MNEMONIC_TO_URL map (SNOMEDCT_US, RXNORM, LNC, ICD10CM, ICD9CM, CPT, CVX, ATC, HCPCS, NDC, MEASURE) in in_process_adapter.py and applied it inside _normalize_system BEFORE SystemResolver.normalize. Updated test assertion to expect http://snomed.info/sct.

issues.spec_citation: FDD §3b 'Row load' (parameterized query discipline) and FDD §3d (translation-time SQL emission)
issues.evidence: fhir4ds/cql/translator/expressions/_functions.py:1581-1599 — `_translate_descendents_closure` builds the closure-table SELECT via f-string interpolation: `sys_sql = SQLRaw(raw_sql=f"'{sys_n.replace(chr(39), chr(39)+chr(39))}'").to_sql()` and `code_sql = SQLRaw(raw_sql=f"'{code.replace(chr(39), chr(39)+chr(39))}'").to_sql()`, then embeds them in a WHERE clause via `f"WHERE _tc.ancestor_system = {sys_sql} AND _tc.ancestor_code = {code_sql}"`. The manual single-quote doubling IS correct and prevents the standard SQL-injection escape vector, but the pattern is brittle compared to the project's otherwise-consistent parameterized-query discipline (e.g., closure.py:300-305 correctly uses `executemany` with `?` placeholders for INSERT, and the inline `_emit_closure_aware_codes_equivalent` / `_translate_code_is_op` paths use `SQLLiteral(value=...).to_sql()` which delegates parameter formatting to the SQL builder). Seed values come from a parsed CQL Library AST (codes), so the practical attack surface is limited to untrusted CQL libraries — but a defense-in-depth stance would route these through `SQLLiteral(...).to_sql()` (the pattern used in the sibling `_translate_code_is_op` method at lines 5424-5434) so the escape responsibility lives in one place.
issues.resolution: Converted f-string SQL emission in _translate_descendents_closure to use SQLLiteral(...).to_sql() pattern matching _translate_code_is_op. The two manual chr(39)+chr(39) f-string interpolations (sys_sql, code_sql) now go through SQLLiteral(value=...).to_sql(), which performs identical single-quote doubling via types.py:268. Generated SQL is byte-identical for all current inputs; escape responsibility now lives in one place.

issues.spec_citation: FDD Phase 4 INV-6: 'deterministic Condition ids' — code-review brief specifies hash inputs '(source_ref, span_start, span_end, system, code) or similar' to be unique per span and deterministic across runs.
issues.evidence: fhir4ds/cql/loader/notes_pipeline.py:340-348 — the deterministic Condition id digest input is `[salt, source_ref, span_start, span_end, code]`. The code system (e.g. SNOMEDCT_US → http://snomed.info/sct) is NOT included. Two affirmed concepts with the same code string from different code systems (e.g. a local/proprietary code '73211009' vs the SNOMED code '73211009') extracted from the same source resource + same span would produce byte-identical Condition ids, causing the second Condition to be silently dropped by the loader's (id, resourceType) dedup (fhir_loader.py:380-387 / 410-416). Fix: include `str(system)` (the post-normalization canonical URL is preferable so mnemonic-vs-URL variants don't diverge) in the sha256 input alongside code: `digest_input = "␟".join([_ID_SALT, fragment.source_ref, str(span_start), str(span_end), str(system), str(code)])`. Low real-world probability for the default UMLS-only setup, but the spec calls for system in the hash.
issues.resolution: Added the post-normalization canonical system URL to the deterministic Condition id digest. Hash inputs are now (salt, source_ref, span_start, span_end, system, code) so two concepts from different code systems at the same span on the same source no longer collide and get silently dropped by loader (id, resourceType) dedup. The INV-6 contract is updated; existing id-determinism tests still pass since they assert length/equality/inequality, not literal hash values.
issues.verified_in: fhir4ds/cql/tests/unit/loader/test_notes_pipeline.py::test_deterministic_id_differs_across_code_systems_at_same_span (new regression test, passes); 105/105 loader unit tests; 1388/1388 cql unit tests; 2822/2822 conformance.

issues.spec_citation: None (performance hygiene). Handoff §7 already flags this as a REV-002 candidate.
issues.evidence: fhir4ds/cql/loader/notes_pipeline.py:436-445 — `_medterm4ds_engine_version()` is a module-level function called from `_build_condition` (line 310 via `engine_version=_medterm4ds_engine_version()`). It invokes `importlib.metadata.version('medterm4ds')` for EVERY derived Condition built. In a batch load over thousands of notes the lookup is repeated per-Condition. `importlib.metadata.version` does a filesystem walk of installed dist-info directories on some Python versions; cheap per-call but not free. Fix: cache the version string on the pipeline instance once in `_ensure_medterm4ds()` (next to `self._medterm4ds_index_version`) and read from `self._medterm4ds_engine_version` in `_build_condition`.
issues.resolution: Promoted _medterm4ds_engine_version from a module-level function to a cached instance method NotesPipeline._medterm4ds_engine_version(). The first call resolves the medterm4ds version via importlib.metadata.version and caches it on self._medterm4ds_engine_version_cached (Optional[str]); all subsequent derived Conditions reuse the cached value. Batch loads over 10k notes now perform one lookup, not 10k+.
issues.verified_in: fhir4ds/cql/tests/unit/loader/test_notes_pipeline.py::test_medterm4ds_engine_version_cached_per_instance (new test, passes); 105/105 loader unit tests; 1388/1388 cql unit tests.

issues.spec_citation: None (maintainability). FDD §0 INV-7 says 'use Phase 1's mnemonic→URL logic'.
issues.evidence: fhir4ds/cql/loader/notes_pipeline.py:422-428 — `_normalize_system` imports `_SOURCE_MNEMONIC_TO_URL` (underscore-prefixed = module-private) from `fhir4ds.cql.terminology.in_process_adapter`. Phase 4 now depends on a Phase 1 implementation detail; renaming or moving the map silently breaks the pipeline's system normalization (the lazy `except ImportError` masks the breakage by degrading to no-expansion, which would emit non-canonical Coding.system URLs without any visible error). Fix: promote the mnemonic map to a shared public module (e.g. `fhir4ds/cql/terminology/mnemonics.py`) and import from there in both `in_process_adapter` and `notes_pipeline`.
issues.resolution: Promoted the mnemonic->URL table to a shared public module: fhir4ds/cql/terminology/system_mappings.py exports SOURCE_MNEMONIC_TO_URL (no underscore). Both in_process_adapter.py and notes_pipeline.py import from the new canonical location. in_process_adapter.py keeps a _SOURCE_MNEMONIC_TO_URL alias to the public map for backward compat with any internal references. Grep confirms no other files imported the old private name.
issues.verified_in: Grep across the repo shows zero remaining private-name imports outside in_process_adapter.py's backward-compat alias; 1388/1388 cql unit tests pass; 2822/2822 conformance.
